objectives.text: act out the conversation about a gazelle that begins “I'm reading a book about animals.”
name animals and describing words: cheetah, rhinoceros, hippopotamus, slow, heavy
compare two animals with -er and than: “The giraffe is faster than the deer.”
tell which animal is the fastest or heaviest, like “The cheetah is the fastest.”
read “The Slow Sloth” from Costa Rica and tell facts about how the sloth lives
act out the shoe shop conversation that begins “Can I try on these shoes?”
name things and describing words: earrings, helmet, necklace, expensive, colorful
compare two things with more, like “This puzzle is more difficult.”
ask and answer “Which sneakers are the most comfortable?” using the most
read “The Most Popular Flavor” from Belgium and tell what it says about the favorite flavor

units.title: School Link 1 · Wonders of the world

objectives.text: learn about famous wonders of the world and where they are
write a report about a special place in Korea
write complete sentences that start with a capital letter and end with a period
tell the class why their special place is worth a visit
act out the concert invitation that begins “My school band is having a concert.”
name music and sports activities: play the cello, practice the violin, play badminton
ask and answer “How often does he play basketball?” with once, twice or three times a week
say how often they practice something, like “I practice twice a week.”
read “Team Sports” from the USA and tell the main idea in their own words
act out the baseball game conversation that begins “Look! Matt is next.”
name kinds of people and how they act: a quick runner, a careful driver, a loud drum player
turn “He's a slow runner” into “He runs slowly,” using words like quickly and loudly
ask and answer “How does she eat?” with “She eats quickly.”
read “The Talent Show” from South Africa and retell what happens at the show
learn about string instruments and how they make sounds
name string instruments like the violin, cello and guitar and tell how they are played
find the naming part and the telling part of a sentence
write a report about a musical instrument
act out the hula hoop conversation that begins “I don't know how to hula hoop.”
encourage a friend with “Don't worry. I'll show you.” and “You're doing great!”
name field day events: have a sack race, play tug-of-war, run in a race, play Frisbee
ask and answer “What are they going to do?” with “They're going to run in a race.”
read “Field Day” from Canada and compare it with field day at their school
act out the packing conversation that begins “Tomorrow is our camping trip.”
name camping activities: set up a tent, build a campfire, go canoeing, catch fireflies
ask and answer “What's he going to do?” and “Are they going to look at the stars?”
tell a partner what they are going to do on a camping trip
retell the main events of “Catching Fireflies” from Argentina in order
learn how muscles and bones work together to move the body
show how a muscle pulls on a bone when they bend an arm
write a report about the muscles that bend and straighten their arms and legs
write telling sentences and asking sentences with the right end marks
act out the dinner table conversation that begins “Pass me the salt, please.”
offer and turn down food politely: “Would you like some more?” “No, thanks. I'm full.”
name chores: mow the lawn, do the laundry, set the table, take out the garbage
ask and answer “What does she have to do?” with “She has to mow the lawn.”
read “Morning Chores” from Singapore and compare the chores with their own
act out the spring cleaning conversation that begins “The weather is so nice!”
name cleaning jobs: dust the furniture, mop the floor, sweep the floor, wipe the table
tell cleaning steps in order with first, next and after that
ask and answer “What will she do first?” and “Will they dust the furniture next?”
read “Our Clean Classroom” from Japan and tell how the class keeps the room clean
learn why recycling matters and which things can be recycled
make a parachute from a plastic bag by following the steps
write commands and exclamations, like “Tie the strings.” and “Look, it's flying!”
tell a partner how to reuse something instead of throwing it away
act out the museum trip conversation that begins “We're going to the museum today.”
ask and answer “How long will it take by subway?” with “It'll take about 20 minutes.”
name ways to travel: take the subway, take a taxi, take the tram, ride a motorcycle
ask and answer “How does he get to work?” with “He takes a bus to work.”
read “The Convenient T-money Card” and explain how the card helps people in Korea
act out the conversation about birthday invitations that begins “Do you need help with the invitation cards?”
name party jobs: bake a cake, make a banner, order pizza, wrap the gift
tell what is done and not done yet, like “She has baked the cake already.”
ask and answer “Has he wrapped the gift yet?” with “Yes, he has” or “No, he hasn't”
read “Making a Birthday Card” and follow the steps in order
learn about the Sumerians and the wheel they made long ago
name things with wheels and tell how a wheel makes work easier
write a report about where wheels are used
fix unfinished sentences by adding the missing part to make a whole sentence
act out the sandwich-making conversation that begins “I'm getting hungry.”
use a lot of, a few and a little with foods like cookies, hot dogs and fruit
ask and answer “How many sandwiches are there?” and “How much ice cream is there?”
tell when to use how many, like cookies, and how much, like ice cream
read “All-Fruit Popsicles” from Spain and tell what they learned about the popsicles
act out the conversation with check questions like “These are new sneakers, aren't they?”
name sense and describing words: smell, taste, sound, delicious, awful, soft
ask and answer “How does the music sound?” with “It sounds wonderful.”
describe a food with look, smell and taste, like “It smells good.”
read “My Dad's Bakery” from France and tell which senses the writer uses

units.title: School Link 6 · The five senses and the brain

objectives.text: learn how the five senses send messages to the brain
write a report about different foods and tastes, like sweet, salty and sour
write questions that start with who, what, where or how and end with a question mark
tell which sense they use to learn about each food
